# Analysis environment (CPU): analysis/, analysis/rlvr/, figures/,
# training/checks/ and the unit tests of collection/, design/ and
# training/midtrain/.
#
# Versions as measured in the environment that produced the paper's analysis
# outputs: Python 3.13.12. These pins need Python 3.12 or later (numpy 2.5.1
# has no release for older versions).
#
# The figure PDFs are pixel-identical to the published ones only with the same
# Matplotlib version and the same font resolution. The generators ask for the
# first available of Nimbus Roman No9 L, Times New Roman and DejaVu Serif; the
# published figures were drawn on a system with neither of the first two
# installed, so Matplotlib used its bundled DejaVu Serif. With another version
# or font the figures are equivalent but not pixel-identical. The numbers do
# not depend on the fonts.
#
# The RLVR analysis (analysis/rlvr/) was run with the Python of the
# post-training image instead (Python 3.10, numpy 1.26.4, pandas 2.2.3; see
# env/posttrain/pip-freeze.txt).

numpy==2.5.1
scipy==1.17.1
matplotlib==3.10.8
pandas==3.0.1
pyarrow==23.0.1
# Only for figures/compare_with_paper.py (renders PDFs for the comparison).
pypdfium2==5.6.0

# Checks and tests.
# training/checks/compare_configs.py, training/midtrain/tests/test_prepare_stage2_assets.py
pyyaml==6.0.3
pytest==9.0.2
# Imported by the collection library that the collection tests load.
zstandard==0.25.0
requests==2.32.5
# numba: the measured environment has numba 0.61.2 installed, but that release
# requires numpy<2.3 and does not import with numpy 2.5, so it cannot be pinned
# here (pip refuses the combination). collection/olmo2_midtrain_membership.py
# then uses its pure-NumPy fallback, which the collection tests compare with the
# numba path. Install numba in the collection environment
# (env/collection/requirements.txt), where it is used for the corpus scan.

# Optional, not installed by default:
# torch (CPU build) - only for training/checks/compare_hf_branches.py
#   pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
# wandb - only for training/checks/check_lr_schedule.py (reads the run's
#   offline Weights & Biases log)
